title: Reconcile AccountManagementService.signOut()'s documented 'soft sign-out' with its always-hard-sign-out callers

evidence.quote:
/// Soft sign-out — clears the in-app session so the user sees the
  /// account picker on next launch, but leaves Firebase's cached

// Hard sign-out: clear Firebase session so the user must re-authenticate
    // on next launch rather than being silently resumed via cached token.

why: AccountManagementService.signOut()'s doc comment claims it deliberately keeps the Firebase token cached specifically so Epic 21.9 AC2 (tap an account tile → dashboard in <200ms) keeps working. Its only two callers (showSignOutConfirmation, showDeleteLocalAccountFlow, both in account_actions.dart) immediately follow it with a genuinely hard authRepositoryProvider.signOut()/authStateProvider.notifier.signOut(), so the fast-resume behavior the comment describes is unreachable from Settings > Sign Out today. This is a stale/misleading comment rather than a functional bug (the actual hard sign-out is arguably the safer choice for an explicit Sign Out action), but it risks a future edit assuming the token survives this call, and no sign-out path anywhere in this batch tells the user whether unsynced changes are pending before ending the session.
recommendation: Update the doc comment to reflect that Settings > Sign Out is always hard, and note where (if anywhere) the soft path is actually exercised — or restore the soft path for the scenario it was designed for.
acceptance_criteria: Doc comment on AccountManagementService.signOut() matches an actual, tested call path, or the soft/hard distinction is removed from the comment.

corrections: AU-4 tag is a loose fit — this is a stale-comment/doc-accuracy issue, not stream-vs-bare-currentUser session routing; no AU-1..5 rule precisely covers 'keep doc comments in sync with behavior.' Doesn't undermine the finding's accuracy or appropriately-minimal severity.
